Robert graduated from Bradley University with degrees in Journalism and Game Design with a minor in Film Studies. Robert tries his best to keep up with all the latest movie releases, from those released in theaters to those released on streaming. While he doesn't always keep up with the latest TV shows, he makes it a goal to watch nearly every major new release possible. He has been honing his craft and following any and all movie news all his life, leading up to now, where he has a vast knowledge of film and film history. Superhero stories have always found success in the medium of film, yet the 21st century has certainly seen a massive explosion of popularity and prominence for these stories of titanic greater-than-average heroes. Between the massive extended universes and the abundance of reliance on intellectual property in general, Superhero movies have become one of the premiere genres of blockbuster film in the past 26 years.

One specific element that has made superhero movies one of the more successful genres of the modern age is their overwhelming fun factor. Between the cartoonish antics and absurdity of these heroes and the larger trends of comedy, many of the best, most crowd-pleasing superhero movies of the modern age find ways to be incredibly fun in their filmmaking and execution. These aren't the only incredibly fun superhero movies of the 21st century, and they certainly won't be the last, but they often come to mind when considering which superhero movies delighted audiences with their overwhelming fun factor.
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/shazam-zachary-levi-stands-at-convenience-store-counter-shazam.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: Shazam (Zachary Levi) stands at the convenience store counter in Shazam! (2019).

blocks.x: Image via Warner Bros. Pictures

The DCEU largely had a reputation of being the more serious, overly gritty extended superhero universe, especially with films like Batman v Superman having as dark of an execution as possible. However, one of the few detractors of this trend in a superhero movie that largely aimed for a style of cheesy, 80s adventure fun was Shazam. Following a young teenage protagonist, it combines classic superhero comedy with coming-of-age elements to create a surprisingly fun time and one of the most underrated DC films.

Zachary Levi gives a fun, committed performance at the center; the characters are charming and likable, and the film understands the inherent fun and power fantasy that comes with being a superhero. It certainly at times feels like DC largely copying and following in the footsteps of what made MCU action comedies work, but it has enough of its own identity thanks to director David F. Sandberg that it's one of the few DCEU films to actually stand the test of time.

7
'The Lego Batman Movie' (2017)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/batman-will-arnett-fires-his-grappling-gun-the-lego-batman-movie.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: Batman (Will Arnett) fires his grappling gun in The Lego Batman Movie

blocks.x: Image via Warner Bros.

Considering the fact that the original The Lego Movie was one of the biggest unexpected surprises and most fun family movies of the 21st century, it would make sense that they continued this charm for the prominent side-character, Lego Batman. The aptly titled The Lego Batman Movie doesn't worry about connecting to other Lego movies, instead telling its own standalone Batman parody story that acts as a hilarious comedic love letter to Batman as a character and his history in film.

It's jam-packed with cartoon antics, all sorts of fun stop-motion action, and a lot of the same visual charm that made the original Lego Movie such a breakaway hit. Especially for fans of Batman as a character, The Lego Batman Movie has a lot to offer, not just in terms of overwhelming Easter eggs and references to previous Batman stories, but a lighthearted story of growth and teamwork where Batman learns to accept the help and camaraderie of those around him.

6
'Deadpool 2' (2018)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/deadpool-2.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2
blocks.c: Deadpool and X Force about to jump from a plane in Deadpool 2.

blocks.x: Image via 20th Century Studios
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress%2Fwp-content%2Fauthors%2F672d316a30cbb-profile%20nov%202024.jpg?fit=crop&w=90&h=90

A trilogy of wildly chaotic superhero parodies befitting the comic icon that they're adapting, each film in the Deadpool trilogy has its own charms and strengths as some of the most fun, satisfyingly bloodsoaked superhero movies ever made. In terms of the raw fun-factor, however, it's hard to deny the stature of Deadpool 2 as the most fun film in the Deadpool trilogy. Without having to rely on setting up Deadpool's origin story or acclimating him into the MCU, Deadpool 2 focuses squarely on what makes Deadpool great: R-rated action with great choreography and raunchy jokes.

The film is constantly playing with the audiences' expectations for a sequel and toying with the conventions of superhero movies as a whole, whether it be through the introduction and immediate killing of the X-Force or the fanboying to reveals of characters like Juggernaut. It's a superhero sequel designed for the overwhelming cultural dominance that the grnre was experiencing in the late 2010s, with the great action directing of David Leitch pushing it over the edge as one of the most fun superhero movies of that era.

5
'Spider-Man' (2002)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/spider-man-2002-poster.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2
blocks.c: Spider-Man swinging across New York in the 2002 movie.

blocks.x: Image via Sony Pictures Releasing

Spider-Man as a character has been at the center of a wide-array of memorable and incredibly fun superhero blockbusters during the 21st century, yet there's something special and truly timeless about the vision of the character brought to life by Sam Raimi nearly 25 years ago. With overwhelming charm and passion oozing from every aspect of its filmmaking, 2002's Spider-Man is about as perfect and exceptionally fun as a superhero origin story can get.

Tobey Maguire's take on Peter Parker is incredibly endearing and fun to watch, on top of Willem Dafoe's Green Goblin being one of the most entertaining villains not just in terms of superhero movies, but in all blockbuster filmmaking in the 21st century. Still, it's the direction and signature charm of Raimi's directing that set Spider-Man apart from other adaptations of the character, as his angle for action and wild camera movements made the film a massive crowd-pleaser full of personality and fun.

4
'Avengers: Endgame' (2019)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/avengers-endgame-chris-evans.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: Captain America holding Mjolnir in Avengers: Endgame

blocks.x: Image via Marvel Studios

In terms of a superhero film designed from the ground up to appeal to fans and garner a massive reaction as a true event, Avengers: Endgame is the type of climactic, entertaining event that cannot easily be compared to other superhero movies. It pays off over a decade of storytelling in the MCU, calling back to all different parts of its past while also setting up for the future in a glorious love-letter to fans. Especially for those that stood with the MCU since the beginning, it's one of the most fun and bombastic experiences that cinema has to offer.

Throughout its 3-hour runtime, the film goes all out in delivering a passionate, incredibly fun experience tailored to the fans that have stuck with the MCU during this time. It all comes together for one of the most epic battle scenes in a superhero movie, where the action is firing off on all fronts and memorable moments are constantly happening one after another. There's a reason that the film became so successful that it was once the highest-grossing movie of all time.

3
'The Incredibles' (2004)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/the-incredibles-jungle-scene.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2
blocks.c: The Parr family in their supersuits stand in action poses with plants behind in The Incredibles

blocks.x: Image via Pixar Animation Studios
https://static0.colliderimages.com/assets/images/sr-db-logo-icon-colored-dark.svg?v=1.9

Largely thanks to the absolute dominance of Marvel and DC superheroes in wider pop culture, so many audiences forget that fan-favorite Pixar film The Incredibles is technically in the conversation when it comes to amazing and fun superhero movie experiences. In that regard, The Incredibles is easily one of the most effective and endlessly entertaining original superhero movies ever made, having an overwhelming appeal for both younger audiences and seasoned superhero fans.

The Parr family are incredibly endearing as far as superheroes are concerned, as well as the 50s-style worldbuilding and adding a lot of charm to the film as a whole. It does this perfect balancing act of having lots of fun that can charm as a family movie while also having exceptional deeper messaging and character development that adults can latch onto. This timeless icon of 2000s animation is still incredibly fun to watch nowadays, with its reputation as one of Pixar's best being wholly deserved.

2
'Guardians of the Galaxy' (2014)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/guardians-of-the-galaxy.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: The Guardians of the Galaxy standing together in the prison breakout scene.

blocks.x: Image via Marvel Studios

While so many entries in the MCU have employed this mixture of comedy and action that has made them incredibly fun blockbusters, yet this signature style is arguably at its best and most entertaining in James Gunn's original Guardians of the Galaxy. The film took what were previously a bunch of largely unknown characters and turned them into absolute icons of sci-fi blockbusters, with overwhelming charm and wit making it one of the biggest success stories of the MCU.

The film is still highly celebrated as one of the best MCU films largely thanks to the absolute fun that it is to experience, with the goofy dynamics and chemistry between these memorable characters massively elevating the film into sci-fi classic status. It brought about a sense of fun and lighthearted joy mixed with genuine emotional heart that became so popular that it completely changed the approach for subsequent MCU films and the superhero genre as a whole.

1
'Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse' (2018)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/spider-man-into-the-spider-verse.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2
blocks.c: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse - Miles and Peter sit and think in their Spidey costumes

blocks.x: Image via Sony Pictures Releasing

With groundbreaking stylized 3D animation and an overwhelming love for Spider-Man as a character, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is one of the biggest fan-favorite movies that the superhero genre has ever released. Its abundance of fun moments and personality-filled character make it an absolute blast from start to finish. From the wild antics of a washed-up Peter Parker teaching the next generation of Spider-Man to its goofy multiverse antics, it's a film that keeps on delivering in terms of charm and fun.

The stylish animation plays a major part in the film's lasting appeal and fun factor, as it makes every joke and action sequence pop and be that much more invigorating. It's simultanously a perfect love-letter for fans of Spider-Man while also being this exceptional standalone story that soars and stands all its own as a wildly fun time. The film is easily in the conversation for not just being the most fun superhero movie, but one of the most fun movies that has ever been released.

'Avengers: Endgame' (2019)

Image via Marvel Studios

In terms of a superhero film designed from the ground up to appeal to fans and garner a massive reaction as a true event, Avengers: Endgame is the type of climactic, entertaining event that cannot easily be compared to other superhero movies. It pays off over a decade of storytelling in the MCU, calling back to all different parts of its past while also setting up for the future in a glorious love-letter to fans. Especially for those that stood with the MCU since the beginning, it's one of the most fun and bombastic experiences that cinema has to offer.

Throughout its 3-hour runtime, the film goes all out in delivering a passionate, incredibly fun experience tailored to the fans that have stuck with the MCU during this time. It all comes together for one of the most epic battle scenes in a superhero movie, where the action is firing off on all fronts and memorable moments are constantly happening one after another. There's a reason that the film became so successful that it was once the highest-grossing movie of all time.

'The Incredibles' (2004)

Image via Pixar Animation Studios

Largely thanks to the absolute dominance of Marvel and DC superheroes in wider pop culture, so many audiences forget that fan-favorite Pixar film The Incredibles is technically in the conversation when it comes to amazing and fun superhero movie experiences. In that regard, The Incredibles is easily one of the most effective and endlessly entertaining original superhero movies ever made, having an overwhelming appeal for both younger audiences and seasoned superhero fans.

The Parr family are incredibly endearing as far as superheroes are concerned, as well as the 50s-style worldbuilding and adding a lot of charm to the film as a whole. It does this perfect balancing act of having lots of fun that can charm as a family movie while also having exceptional deeper messaging and character development that adults can latch onto. This timeless icon of 2000s animation is still incredibly fun to watch nowadays, with its reputation as one of Pixar's best being wholly deserved.

2
'Guardians of the Galaxy' (2014)

Image via Marvel Studios

While so many entries in the MCU have employed this mixture of comedy and action that has made them incredibly fun blockbusters, yet this signature style is arguably at its best and most entertaining in James Gunn's original Guardians of the Galaxy. The film took what were previously a bunch of largely unknown characters and turned them into absolute icons of sci-fi blockbusters, with overwhelming charm and wit making it one of the biggest success stories of the MCU.

The film is still highly celebrated as one of the best MCU films largely thanks to the absolute fun that it is to experience, with the goofy dynamics and chemistry between these memorable characters massively elevating the film into sci-fi classic status. It brought about a sense of fun and lighthearted joy mixed with genuine emotional heart that became so popular that it completely changed the approach for subsequent MCU films and the superhero genre as a whole.

1
'Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse' (2018)

Image via Sony Pictures Releasing

With groundbreaking stylized 3D animation and an overwhelming love for Spider-Man as a character, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is one of the biggest fan-favorite movies that the superhero genre has ever released. Its abundance of fun moments and personality-filled character make it an absolute blast from start to finish. From the wild antics of a washed-up Peter Parker teaching the next generation of Spider-Man to its goofy multiverse antics, it's a film that keeps on delivering in terms of charm and fun.

The stylish animation plays a major part in the film's lasting appeal and fun factor, as it makes every joke and action sequence pop and be that much more invigorating. It's simultanously a perfect love-letter for fans of Spider-Man while also being this exceptional standalone story that soars and stands all its own as a wildly fun time. The film is easily in the conversation for not just being the most fun superhero movie, but one of the most fun movies that has ever been released.
